appraisal_events.evidence: « Je ne peux pas dire comme je trouve que Swann change... il est d'un vieux ! » ... « Je crois qu'il a beaucoup de soucis avec sa coquine de femme qui vit au su de tout Combray avec un certain monsieur de Charlus. C'est la fable de la ville. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The family's table talk after Swann's departure records his visible decline and treats his wife's public infidelity as town gossip, locally lowering him even as the grandfather insists he no longer loves her.

appraisal_events.evidence: mon père... dit à ma mère : « Va donc avec lui... reste un peu dans sa chambre » ... j'avais réussi... à détendre sa volonté, à faire fléchir sa raison... [ce qui] m'élevait à la dignité de grande personne et m'avait fait atteindre tout d'un coup à une sorte de puberté du chagrin, d'émancipation des larmes.
appraisal_events.explanation: Against all expectation of punishment, the father's sudden leniency grants the narrator his mother's presence for the night; the narrator explicitly reads this as a personal triumph that elevates him to adult dignity, even while recognizing it as won at the cost of his mother's usual firmness.

status_effects.explanation: His wife's public infidelity is discussed as common town knowledge (« la fable de la ville »), locally diminishing his standing within the family's report of social opinion.

He attains the coveted closeness to his mother he had despaired of, and explicitly experiences this as pride and elevation to the dignity of a grown person, the dominant local outcome despite his simultaneous guilt.

Normally barred from his mother's company past bedtime and expecting expulsion to boarding school for his transgression, he is instead admitted to have her spend the whole night in his room, crossing a boundary of parental intimacy usually closed to him.
She departs from her habitual firmness and is explicitly described as yielding, « s'avouait vaincue », her educational resolve bending under the narrator's emotional pressure.

ambiguities: The narrator explicitly frames his mother's staying the night as both a personal triumph elevating him and a source of guilt over her loss of resolve; per the consummation/renewal guidance, the dominant attained outcome is read as positive for the narrator even though the passage devotes substantial weight to his ambivalence and to his mother's yielding.
